hardwareHubs.note: Newlab runs a hardware startup campus with technical labs and shops at the Brooklyn Navy Yard.
More than 100 optics and photonics companies in the Finger Lakes region were reported in 2014.
Cornell runs the Rev: Ithaca Startup Works hardware accelerators.

makerspaces.name: Fat Cat Fab Lab
makerspaces.note: Volunteer-run space in the West Village listing 3D printing, laser cutting, wood and metal shops, electronics and CNC routing.

makerspaces.name: NYC Resistor
makerspaces.note: Hacker collective space whose site documents a laser cutter.

makerspaces.name: Rochester Makerspace
makerspaces.note: Lists a machine shop, 3D printers, CNC routers, a laser cutter and electronics equipment.

events.name: Maker Faire Long Island
events.note: Ninth annual edition announced for 2026 at Stony Brook University.

programs.name: Newlab
programs.note: Offers hardware startups technical labs, shops, workspaces and access to venture and non-dilutive capital.

programs.name: Rev: Ithaca Startup Works Prototyping Hardware Accelerator
programs.note: Summer program with Cornell Engineering that gives product teams a prototyping stipend of up to 2,000 dollars.

specialties.name: Optics and photonics
specialties.note: The University of Rochester Institute of Optics was the first in the US and the region hosts over 100 optics firms.

specialties.name: Integrated photonics manufacturing
specialties.note: The AIM Photonics institute is a 600 million dollar public-private partnership based in the state.

specialties.name: Semiconductors
specialties.note: GlobalFoundries moved its headquarters to Malta, where its Fab 8 chip plant operates.

support.name: NY MEP (statewide center FuzeHub plus ten regional centers)
support.note: Run through Empire State Development, with FuzeHub as the statewide center offering assessments, CAD design and funding programs.

support.name: FuzeHub
support.note: Statewide MEP network site listing manufacturing grants, a hardware prototyping workshop and an innovation fund.
